newsitem.title: USA: Shiva switch selected by Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Shiva switch selected by Telekom.

text.p: Shiva Corp said Thurday that Deutsche Telekom, Europe's largest telecommunications provider, had chosen the Shiva LanRover Access Switch as part of its system for providing customers with Internet access.
Shiva said Deutsche Telekom had signed a letter of intent and a contract is expected to be signed by the end of month.
The deal will enable Deutsche Telekom to offer new Internet services to its customers via Shiva's LanRover switch in the first quarter of 1997, the equipment provider said.
Shiva stock gained 1-1/8 to 20-3/8 Thursday morning.
The share price rise represents only a slight rebound from Wednesday's share price plunge.

In extremely heavy trading, Shiva stock fell 15-5/8, or 45 percent, to 19-1/4 after the company said late Tuesday that it expected earnings for the fourth quarter of 1996 to be only about a third of Wall Street's consensus expectations.
The deal with Telekom, if completed, would represent a vote of confidence in Shiva's switching product line-up.

Among the concerns cited by analysts for the sheer drop in Shiva's stock price Wednesday were fears that the company faced rising competition in the fast-growing market for remote access switching equipment used by Internet Service providers.
Shiva competes with companies like Ascend Communications Inc, Cascade Communications Corp and U.S. Robotics Corp in this area.

"This agreement with Deutsche Telekom, which is Europe's largest telecommunications company and the third largest carrier worldwide, is evidence of Shiva's continued success in the global ISP market," said Frank Ingari, Shiva's president and chief executive, of Thursday's tenative deal.
